note: From the City of Nashua, its departments and local news, checked Oct 28, 2026. Every item links to its source.

nashua.note: All home types; Redfin calls the market very competitive. For single-family homes only, the NH Association of Realtors put Nashua's August median at $615,000, up 11.8% from $549,950 and tied with June's record (Nashua Ink Link, Sep 13).

region.source: New Hampshire Association of Realtors, reported by Nashua Ink Link
region.towns: New Hampshire statewide. Hillsborough County single-family median: $566,500, down 3.2% from $585,000.

singleFamily.note: Down from a record $580,000 in July. 1,381 closed sales, up 1.6%; 2.8 months of inventory; 27 days on market.

condo.note: Statewide condos and townhouses. 420 closed sales, down 3.2%; 38 days on market, up from 28.

region.summary: New Hampshire, August 2026 (New Hampshire Association of Realtors, reported by Nashua Ink Link): single-family median $569,900 (+3.6%), condos $434,900 (+4.3%). Hillsborough County single-family median: $566,500, down 3.2% from $585,000.

business.note: Openings and closures come from local news coverage (Nashua Independent, Concord Monitor, 97.5 WOKQ, Nashua Ink Link), not from the city. Nashua Telegraph business stories are mostly paywalled and were not used.

openings.name: Mesozoic Tiki Bar & Lounge
openings.what: Tiki bar and lounge with wood-fired pizza
openings.detail: Opened at 97 Main St in the former Flight Center space with a public soft opening in late August. Live entertainment was set to start in mid-September.

openings.name: Greater Nashua Mental Health, Pine Street site
openings.detail: Opened at 3 Pine St. Ext., bringing intake, substance use, justice, older adult and deaf and hard of hearing services back under one roof. A Feb 2 gas explosion destroyed its building at 440 Amherst St.

openings.name: Southern New Hampshire Health Pharmacy
openings.what: Retail pharmacy, the health system's first
openings.detail: Recently opened inside Southern New Hampshire Medical Center and open to non-patients. Hours: Monday to Friday 7 am to 7 pm, Saturday 7 am to noon.

openings.name: Predictive Monitor headquarters
openings.what: Life sciences tech company that monitors lab refrigeration
openings.detail: Held a ribbon cutting and open house at its new 15,000 sq ft headquarters, a building it bought at 1800 Southwood Drive, after renting a smaller space.

closures.name: Fresh of Nashua
closures.what: Downtown women's clothing boutique, open since 2008
closures.detail: Closed for good on August 15 at 3 pm as its owner retired after 18 years.

notices.title: Trick-or-treat is Saturday, October 31, 6 to 8 pm
notices.detail: The city keeps its usual schedule. Anyone driving during those hours should take extra care and watch for children.

notices.title: Election Day: polls open 6 am to 8 pm in all nine wards
notices.detail: You can register at your polling place on Election Day if you are 18 or older, a U.S. citizen and live in the ward. Look up your ward's polling place on the city's Where Do I Vote page. City Clerk: 603-589-3010.

notices.title: No school Nov 3, Nov 11 and Nov 25 to 27
notices.detail: Election Day is a teacher in-service day with no classes. Schools and district offices close for Veterans Day and the Thanksgiving recess.

notices.title: Last household hazardous waste day of 2026 is Saturday, Nov 7
notices.detail: 8 am to noon at 25 Crown St. Limit 10 gallons or 20 pounds per household; a $20 fee per vehicle is requested. Latex paint, used oil, asbestos and smoke detectors are not accepted.

notices.title: Extra Saturday hours for soft yard waste at Four Hills Landfill
notices.detail: Residents only, on Saturdays Nov 7, 14, 21 and 28. The scale closes at 12:45 pm, but soft yard waste is accepted until 4 pm.

notices.title: City Hall closed for Veterans Day, Wednesday, Nov 11
notices.detail: City offices close for the holiday. The closure schedule does not apply to the Nashua Transit System or the Division of Public Works.

notices.title: Veterans Day Parade steps off from Holman Stadium at 11:11 am
notices.detail: Monument ceremonies begin at 8 am. A luncheon for parade participants follows at the Adult Learning Center, 4 Lake St.

notices.title: Trash and recycling run one day late in Veterans Day and Thanksgiving weeks
notices.detail: The Nov 11 and Nov 26 holidays make collection one day late in those weeks. Look up your street's day on the city's schedule map.

notices.title: Aldermen hold a public hearing on R-26-077, Monday, Nov 23, 7 pm
notices.detail: Special Board of Aldermen meeting in the Aldermanic Chamber, City Hall, 229 Main St. The agenda is on the city's CivicClerk portal; the calendar listing does not say what the resolution covers.

notices.title: City Hall closed Thanksgiving Day and the day after, Nov 26 and 27
notices.detail: City offices close both days for the holiday.

notices.title: Main Street closes 2 to 11 pm for the Winter Stroll, Saturday, Nov 28
notices.detail: Downtown parking will be limited. Free shuttles run every 15 minutes from 4 to 9:30 pm from Holman Stadium, the Crown Street Park and Ride and Rivier University's Memorial Hall. The organizer's page still carries some details from last year, so check before you go.

notices.title: Rolling stairwell closures at both downtown garages for about two weeks
notices.detail: Stairwell levels at the Elm Street and High Street garages close in turns; follow posted signs and exit maps. The High Street elevator is out of service and the Elm Street north stairs are closed. Gates are not active yet, so prepay at the kiosks.

notices.title: No overnight parking permit pickup at the City Clerk's Office on Oct 29; back Nov 5
notices.detail: Overnight street parking from midnight to 6 am needs a permit in designated areas; other streets have a two-hour limit. Parking Department: 603-589-3205.

safety.note: Compiled from Nashua Police and Nashua Fire Rescue pages, the 2025 police annual report, Fire Commission minutes and local news. Incidents are described by type, street and date only; no names of people involved.

police.name: Nashua Police Department
police.oversight: Three-member Board of Police Commissioners appointed by the Governor (through the Governor and Executive Council); it hires officers, sets department rules and controls police property.
police.logsNote: Arrest logs and media releases are posted as documents in the department's Document Center. The folder loads by script and individual logs could not be opened this session, so posting frequency and contents are unconfirmed.

recent.title: Arrest in two burglaries
recent.detail: Nashua police arrested a city man on Oct 17 in connection with two alleged burglaries.

recent.title: Stalking and protective order arrest
recent.detail: Police arrested a man accused of domestic violence against a woman who had a protective order against him. He was held without bail.

recent.title: Cocaine possession arrest
recent.detail: Police arrested a man on a cocaine possession charge; he was held pending arraignment in Superior Court.

recent.title: Federal charge after police find pistol converted to fire automatically
recent.detail: Nashua police found a loaded pistol fitted with a 'switch' on Sep 24. A Nashua teen was arrested Oct 4 and federally charged with possessing a machine gun.

recent.title: Arrest for protective order violations and stalking
recent.detail: Police arrested a man on Sep 28 on two counts of violating a protective order and two counts of stalking. He was held without bail.

recent.title: Arson suspect caught after manhunt
recent.detail: After a fire on Sep 21, Nashua police and Tyngsborough, Mass., police searched for a suspect whose vehicle was found in Tyngsborough. He was captured Sep 22 and charged with arson and related offenses.

recent.title: Four drug arrests in August under substance abuse initiative
recent.detail: The Narcotics Intelligence Division and Problem Oriented Policing Unit made four arrests in August sweeps. Residents can report drug activity to the department's drug hotline.

recent.title: Animal cruelty arrest
recent.detail: Police arrested a man on Sep 17 accused of entering an acquaintance's home without permission and injuring a dog. He was held on preventive detention.

programs.name: Citizens Academy
programs.detail: Spring 2026 class ran from April 1 to a May 21 graduation.

programs.name: Problem Oriented Policing Unit
programs.detail: Specialty unit; took part in the 2026 drug sweeps.

programs.name: Drug Hotline
programs.detail: Online form to report drug activity to the Narcotics Intelligence Division.

fire.name: Nashua Fire Rescue
fire.oversight: Elected five-member Board of Fire Commissioners (four-year terms, with seats filled at each municipal election); it handles hiring and promotions, department rules and property.

stats.label: Emergency arrivals in 4 minutes or less

recent.title: Commission approves dispatcher hiring list and supervisor promotion
recent.detail: The board approved a Fire Alarm Operator hiring list and a Fire Alarm Supervisor promotion, and recommended three bond resolutions ahead of an Oct 26 public hearing.

recent.title: Chief looks at shifting an ambulance to daytime
recent.detail: The chief is exploring an agreement with AMR to move an ambulance from nighttime to daytime service, when call demand is higher. Some reserve apparatus is up for sale.

recent.title: Firefighters Memorial Sunday
recent.detail: Annual memorial service at the Firemen's Memorial at 10 a.m.

recent.title: Basement fire damages home on Barnsdale Road
recent.detail: Crews responded around 2:15 p.m. to a fire that started in the basement of a single-story home. The house was heavily damaged; no one was home or hurt.

recent.title: 9/11 25th anniversary ceremony
recent.detail: Ceremony at 70 East Hollis Street marking 25 years since the Sept. 11 attacks.

recent.title: New Engine 1 in service; about 65 apply to be firefighters
recent.detail: A new Engine 1 went into service and reserve Ladder 5 and Engine 1 are being sold. The firefighter application period closed Sep 7 with about 65 applicants.

recent.title: Neighbor slows garage fire on Hughey Street
recent.detail: A neighbor used a garden hose on a garage fire on Aug 29 until firefighters arrived and put it out. The fire did not reach the house and no one was hurt.

recent.title: Two-alarm fire on Lynde Street
recent.detail: A pre-dawn fire engulfed a single-family home; hoarding conditions slowed crews and one firefighter hurt an ankle. Residents got out safely and the Fire Marshal's Office is investigating.

burnPermits.text: Property owners apply online for a free seasonal campfire permit; others call (603) 594-3636 to book a site visit (3 to 5 p.m. daily).

benchmarks.note: FBI figures for 2024, the latest year with matching city, state and national numbers. Rates are offenses reported to police per 100,000 residents. People who work in or shop in Nashua but live elsewhere aren’t counted as residents, which pushes per-resident rates up. The FBI advises against ranking places on these numbers alone.
benchmarks.homeNote: FBI, 2024. Per-resident rates; visitors and commuters aren’t counted as residents.
benchmarks.fireNote: No fire comparison yet: national fire figures don’t match how these departments count calls or staff.
